Definition: Packet Error Rate refers to the frequency at which errors occur during the transmission or reception of data packets in telecommunications.

Name: PF
Definition: Programmable Function refers to a feature or capability that can be customized or configured to perform specific tasks or functions according to user-defined instructions or commands.

Name: PFCP
Definition: Packet Forwarding Control Protocol is a protocol used in telecommunications that is responsible for controlling the forwarding of data packets between network devices.

Name: PFD
Definition: Packet Flow Descriptor is a term used in the field of telecommunications to refer to a detailed specification of the sequence, direction, and characteristics of data packets as they traverse a network. It provides a clear and concise description of how packets are transmitted, routed, and processed within the network infrastructure.

Name: PGI
Definition: Post Good Issue is a task performed by warehouse teams and SAP that releases a device/material for shipment. This task triggers several downstream activities for other teams.

Name: PGU
Definition: A reference of time for when a class of new hire team members start taking calls in the contact centre for the first time.

Name: PGW-C
Definition: P-GW Control Plane Function refers to a specific function within telecommunications networks. It is responsible for controlling and managing various aspects related to the Packet Data Network (PDN) Gateway (P-GW). The control plane function handles tasks such as establishing and terminating connections, authentication and authorization of user sessions, as well as policy enforcement for Quality of Service (QoS) and traffic routing.

Name: PGW-U
Definition: P-GW User Plane Function refers to a component in telecommunications that is responsible for handling the user data traffic between the mobile device and the external networks. It plays a crucial role in routing, forwarding, and processing the data packets without involving the control plane functions.

Name: PH
Definition: Power Headroom in the context of Telecommunications refers to the available margin or capacity of power within a communication system. It represents the difference between the maximum power level that a user equipment (UE) can transmit and the actual power that is being used.

Name: PHI
Definition: Personal health information refers to information that a healthcare professional collects to identify an individual and determine appropriate care. This would include information such as: Claims information Diagnostic results Health Care Number Health history Health info and benefits Medical records Prescription information Treatment information

Name: PHIPA
Definition: Personal Health Information Protection Act refers to a legislation that governs the protection and privacy of personal health information within the context of healthcare. It establishes guidelines and regulations that healthcare providers must adhere to in order to safeguard the confidentiality and security of individuals' health data. This act ensures that personal health information is handled and shared appropriately, protecting the rights and privacy of patients.

Name: PHR
Definition: Power Headroom Report is a term used in telecommunications to refer to a report that provides information about the difference between the maximum transmit power capability of a device or system and the actual power being used. It helps in determining the available power reserve, which can be essential for maintaining a reliable and efficient communication network.

Name: PHY
Definition: Physical Layer is the lowest level of the OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model and refers to the actual hardware and transmission medium used in a network. It is responsible for the physical transmission of data between network devices, without considering the content or structure of the data.

Name: PI
Definition: Any information about an identifiable individual. An individual is “Identifiable” where it is reasonably possible for the individual to be identified by that information alone or in combination with other available information. Personal information can be in any medium - verbal, electronic, written, video, recording, images. Personal health information is always considered to be sensitive personal information, as are certain other types of personal information such as banking and credit information, government issued identification numbers such as drivers’ license, health, or social insurance numbers. Sourced from 2019 THPS data stewardship working session: Any information, directly or indirectly, about or related to an identifiable person (employee, customer, partner, ...). Personal Information Is any information whether available on hard copy or electronic, that would identify a specific individual.

Name: PIA
Definition: The Privacy Impact Assessment is an auditable tool designed to help team members to identify and appropriately mitigate the privacy and security risks associated with their project.

Name: PIC
Definition: The interexchange carrier designated by a voice wireline subscriber to provide direct-dial long distance services on that line; sometimes used as a verb ("to PIC") or adjective ("a PICed provider"). When a subscriber wishes to place a voice wireline long distance call using a non-PICed provider, the subscriber must dial around to access the non-PICed providers network. Sometimes referred to as preselection or presubscription. French: EIB (entreprise intercirconscription de base).

Name: PICH
Definition: Paging Indication Channel refers to a channel in telecommunications that is used to indicate the presence of incoming messages or calls for a specific device.

Name: PII
Definition: Personally Identifiable Information refers to any information that can be used to identify an individual. It typically includes details such as name, social security number, address, date of birth, and contact information. This type of information is sensitive and should be protected to ensure privacy and security.

Name: PIM
Definition: Purchasing and Inventory Management in the context of Telecommunications refers to the systematic process of acquiring telecommunications equipment, devices, and materials necessary for operational activities, as well as efficiently tracking and managing the stock of these items.

Full Name: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act
Name: PIPEDA
Definition: Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act is a legislation that pertains to privacy and security. It sets out rules and regulations for the collection, use, and disclosure of personal information by private sector organizations in Canada. The act aims to establish guidelines that organizations must follow to protect the privacy of individuals and ensure the secure handling of their personal information.

Name: PIR
Definition: The Post Incident Report tab helps you to understand the cause of the major incident, and the actions taken by the teams to resolve the incident.

Name: PIWS
Definition: A Purefibre tier 2 team, which ensures that a technician is dispatched to a customers' home only when absolutely necessary and after all necessary troubleshooting has been completed

Name: PLMN
Definition: Public Land Mobile Network refers to a telecommunications system that allows mobile devices to connect to a cellular network through radio waves, providing communication services such as voice calls, messaging, and data transmission. It is a network infrastructure that enables reliable and seamless mobile communications for the general public, ensuring wide coverage and connectivity across a given geographic area.

Name: PMAA
Definition: Produit moyen mensuel par client. Le calcul tient compte du total des revenus de réseau divisé par le nombre moyen d’abonnés sur le réseau pour le mois. Frais de financement des appareils exclus.

Name: PMF
Definition: Product-Market Fit refers to the method of understanding and successfully identifying a target market (customer segment) to serve with the right product and services.

Name: PMI
Definition: Precoding Matrix Indicator refers to a signaling parameter used in telecommunications. It is a value indicator that determines the specific precoding matrix to be used in wireless transmission.

Name: PMO
Definition: A project management office is a group or department within a business or enterprise that defines and maintains standards for project management within the organization.

Name: PMS
Definition: Pharmacy Management System refers to a computerized system used in healthcare settings to manage and streamline various aspects of pharmacy operations such as inventory management, medication dispensing, and prescription processing.

Name: PNI
Definition: Programs of National Interest are programs that the CRTC has determined should be supported through regulation: dramas, long form documentaries and award shows that support Canadian creativity. There is a CPE for PNI for some broadcasters as well as all Canadian programming.

Name: PO
Definition: Process Optimization refers to the systematic examination and improvement of existing processes in order to enhance efficiency, reduce waste, and streamline operations. It involves identifying bottlenecks, eliminating unnecessary steps, and implementing more effective methods to achieve desired outcomes.

Name: POB
Definition: A contractual promise to transfer a distinct good or service to a customer as part of a revenue arrangement.

Name: PoC
Definition: Proof of Concept refers to a demonstration or experiment conducted to verify the feasibility and viability of a particular idea, concept, or design. It serves as a preliminary test to determine if the concept can be successfully implemented or developed further.

Name: POD
Definition: A demarcation point is the physical point at which a telecommunications company's public network ends and the customer's private network begins.

Name: POE
Definition: Place Of Employment refers to the specific location or establishment where an individual works or is employed.

Name: POM
Definition: The name of unlimited data rate plan.

Name: PON
Definition: Passive Optical Network (PON) refers to a telecommunications system that uses fiber optic cables to transmit data signals. It is a network architecture that enables the transmission of information, such as voice, video, and data, from a central location to multiple end-users. In a PON, signals are distributed passively, meaning they are not amplified or processed along the transmission path. Instead, the network relies on passive components like splitters and couplers to divide and distribute the signals to different users. PONs offer a cost-effective and scalable solution for delivering high-speed internet access and other communication services to residential and business customers.

Name: POR
Definition: A Plan of Record is an approved plan by senior leadership that illustrates an organization's prioritized initiatives and projects.

Name: POTS
Definition: The traditional, analog telephone system that uses copper wires to transmit voice signals.

Full Name: Power Purchase Agreement / Purchase Price Allocation
Name: PPA
Definition: A contract for the sale of electricity, or the accounting process of allocating cost in an acquisition.

Name: PPDR
Definition: Public Protection and Disaster Relief in the context of Telecommunications refers to the proactive measures and emergency response activities undertaken by telecommunication service providers and authorities to ensure public safety and mitigate the impact of disasters on communication networks. It involves implementing strategies, protocols, and technologies to strengthen the resilience, availability, and reliability of telecommunications infrastructure during emergencies and disasters.

Name: PPE
Definition: Process and Performance Excellence in the context of Telecommunications refers to the implementation of highly efficient and effective operational procedures and strategies that result in optimal performance and delivery of services. This encompasses the use of streamlined processes, advanced technology, and continuous improvement initiatives to ensure consistent and reliable telecommunications services without explicitly mentioning specific examples or benefits.

Name: PPI
Definition: Pixels Per Inch (PPI) in the context of Telecommunications refers to the measurement of the pixel density on a screen or display. It indicates the number of individual pixels that are present per inch of the screen.

Name: PPV
Definition: Pay Per View in the context of Telecommunications refers to a system where viewers pay a specific fee to access and watch a particular piece of content, such as a live event or a movie, on their TV or other electronic devices.

Name: PQ
Definition: Priority Queue, in the context of General, refers to a data structure that stores elements with associated priorities, where elements with higher priority are dequeued or accessed before elements with lower priority. It allows for efficient retrieval of the most prioritized element without having to search the entire structure.

Name: PRACH
Definition: Physical Random Access Channel is a dedicated channel allocated in a telecommunications system for allowing devices to access the network randomly without any specific order or sequence.

Name: PRB
Definition: Physical Resource Blocks are a term used in the field of telecommunications to refer to the allocation of frequency resources within a given communication system. They represent a specific amount of frequency and time resources that are assigned to a user for transmitting and receiving data.

Name: PRI
Definition: Prime Rate Interface refers to a specific type of interface utilized in the context of enterprise. It is a method or system through which the prime rate, which is the interest rate offered by commercial banks to their most creditworthy customers, is communicated and made accessible to businesses. This interface allows enterprises to stay informed about the prime rate, which is a crucial factor in determining borrowing costs and financial decisions.

Name: PS
Definition: Packet Switched is a method of data transmission in telecommunications where information is divided into small packets before being sent over a network. Each packet contains a piece of the data being transmitted, along with information on its destination address. These packets are then independently routed across the network to their destination. Unlike traditional circuit-switched networks, which establish a dedicated communication path for the entire duration of a call, packet-switched networks allow for more efficient utilization of network resources by dynamically sharing available bandwidth among multiple users.

Name: PSA
Definition: PDU Session Anchor in the context of Telecommunications refers to the network element that manages and controls the communication sessions between the User Plane Function (UPF) and other network functions. It acts as the central point of control for a specific PDU (Protocol Data Unit) session, handling the establishment, maintenance, and termination of the session. The PDU Session Anchor facilitates the seamless transmission of data and enables efficient routing and management of user traffic within the telecommunications network.

Name: PSCell
Definition: Primary Secondary Cell refers to a concept in telecommunications where a primary cell is a base station that provides the main coverage area for mobile devices, while a secondary cell is an additional base station that enhances coverage or capacity in certain areas.

Name: PSCM
Definition: Program Strategy & Change Management in the context of Enterprise refers to the systematic approach and framework used to plan, execute, and manage large-scale programs and initiatives aimed at driving organizational change. It involves analyzing and aligning program objectives with the overall strategic goals of the enterprise, and implementing effective strategies to manage and mitigate the impact of change on various stakeholders. This involves assessing risks, coordinating resources, communicating with stakeholders, and implementing change management methodologies to ensure successful program delivery and adoption of the desired changes.

Name: PSD
Definition: Power Spectral Density refers to the distribution of power of a signal per unit frequency. It quantifies how the power of a signal is distributed among different frequencies, providing information about the signal's spectral characteristics.

Name: PSE
Definition: A Power Sourcing Equipment is a device that provides power on the Ethernet cable and powers the Powered Device (PD) that accepts the power.

Name: PSIH
Definition: Productive sign-in hours refers to the measurable time when an employee is actively logged into work systems and engaged in productive activities.

Name: PSM
Definition: Power Save Mode in the context of telecommunications refers to a feature or setting that reduces the power consumption of a device to extend its battery life.

Name: PSO
Definition: Team name

Name: PSS
Definition: Primary Synchronization Signal in the context of telecommunications refers to a specific signal used in wireless networks to assist in the synchronization and timing of communication between devices.

Name: PSTN
Definition: Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) refers to the traditional phone system used for telecommunications, which relies on a physical network of copper wires and circuit-switching technology to transmit voice calls.

Name: PTMS
Definition: A system that manages the transfer and handoff of planning data between organizational units or processes.

Name: PTT
Definition: Push-To-Talk refers to a communication method in the field of telecommunications that allows users to initiate instant voice communication with the push of a button.

Name: PTW
Definition: Paging Time Window refers to a specific period within a telecommunications system during which paging messages are transmitted to mobile devices. It is a predefined interval of time allocated for sending paging signals to locate and alert the desired recipient.

Name: PUSCH
Definition: Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) is a telecommunications term that refers to a specific channel in the uplink direction of wireless communication systems. It is designed to allow multiple users to share the same physical resources for transmitting their data to the network. The PUSCH plays a crucial role in enabling efficient and simultaneous transmission of data from multiple users over the wireless network.

Name: PVR
Definition: Personal Video Recorder, in the context of telecommunications, refers to a device that allows users to record television programs for later viewing. It enables users to schedule recordings, pause, rewind, and fast-forward live TV, providing them with flexibility and control over their viewing experience.

Name: PW
Definition: Password in the context of general usage refers to a secret combination of characters used to access a protected website, device, or system.

Name: PWI
Definition: Personal Wellness Information refers to data and details pertaining to an individual's overall health status and self-care practices. It encompasses information related to a person's physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being. This information provides insights into an individual's lifestyle choices, exercise routines, diet, sleep patterns, stress levels, and other factors that contribute to their personal well-being.

Name: PWS
Definition: Public Warning System in the context of Telecommunications refers to a communication infrastructure specifically designed for broadcasting urgent messages and alerts to the general public.

Name: QAM
Definition: Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) refers to a digital modulation technique used in telecommunications. It combines both amplitude modulation and phase modulation to efficiently transmit data over a communication channel. By varying the phase and amplitude of the carrier signal, multiple amplitude levels can be used to represent different digital symbols, allowing for increased data transmission rates. QAM is widely employed in various communication systems, including satellite and cable television, wireless networks, and digital subscriber lines (DSL).

Name: QC-LDPC
Definition: Quasi-Cyclic LDPC, in the context of Telecommunications, refers to a type of Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) code structure. LDPC codes are error correction codes that are used to improve the reliability of data transmission over noisy communication channels. The term "quasi-cyclic" in Quasi-Cyclic LDPC indicates that the code's matrix has a cyclic structure, but with some variation or irregularity in its cyclic properties. It is a systematic way to construct LDPC codes with desirable properties for efficient error correction.

Name: QCI
Definition: A Queue Consolidation Initiative is a strategic business process improvement effort that aims to streamline and combine multiple service queues into a more efficient, unified system.

Name: QFI
Definition: QoS Flow Identifier in the context of Telecommunications refers to a unique identifier assigned to a Quality of Service (QoS) flow within a network. It is used to distinguish and manage different flows of data traffic based on their specific QoS requirements.

Name: QIDC
Definition: Quebec Internet Data Centre refers to a facility located in Quebec that provides infrastructure and services for hosting and managing enterprise data and digital assets.

Name: QoE
Definition: Quality of Experience in the context of Telecommunications refers to the overall perception and satisfaction of users while using telecommunication services.

Name: QoQ
Definition: Quarter-Over-Quarter refers to a comparison of a financial or accounting metric or performance over consecutive quarters. It measures the change or growth in a specific variable or indicator from one quarter to the next, allowing for analysis of trends and patterns in financial data.

Name: QoS
Definition: Quality of Service in the context of telecommunications refers to the measure of performance and reliability of a network or communication service. It focuses on ensuring the delivery of data traffic with consistent and predictable characteristics, such as low latency, high throughput, and minimal packet loss.

Name: QPSK
Definition: Quaternary Phase-Shift Keying is a modulation scheme used in telecommunications. It involves encoding digital information by varying the phase of a carrier signal. Unlike traditional binary phase-shift keying, which uses two phase states to represent data, quaternary phase-shift keying utilizes four different phase states to transmit information.

Name: QSM
Definition: Qualicom Store Manager in the context of Enterprise refers to an individual who is responsible for overseeing the operations and performance of a Qualicom Store. They supervise the day-to-day activities, manage inventory, handle customer inquiries, and ensure that the store meets sales targets and operational goals.

Name: R
Definition: Code Rates in channel coding refer to the ratio of the useful information (data) to the total bandwidth or capacity used for transmission in a telecommunications system. It determines how efficiently the data is encoded and transmitted over the communication channel.

Name: RA
Definition: Routing Area is a geographical region in a telecommunications network where a group of base stations and their corresponding mobile devices are identified and controlled by a specific Mobility Management Entity (MME) or a corresponding network node.

Name: RACH
Definition: Random Access Channel is a telecommunications term that refers to a specific channel used in a communication system, allowing multiple users to independently access the system without any predefined time slots or fixed order of transmission. This channel enables users to initiate communication or transmit data whenever required, providing flexibility and efficient utilization of system resources.

Name: RACI
Definition: Responsibility assignment matrix used in stakeholder management.

Name: RAF
Definition: Refer a Friend in the context of Marketing and Sales refers to a strategy or program implemented by companies to encourage existing customers to recommend their products or services to their friends or acquaintances.

Name: RAN
Definition: The Radio Access Network, often called the cellular network, connects user devices, such as smartphones or smart traffic lights, to the nearest receiving antenna over radio signals, also known as spectrum.

Name: RAR
Definition: Random Access Response refers to a communication protocol used in telecommunications to enable efficient access and allocation of network resources. It is a message sent by the network to a device attempting to establish a connection or transmit data. The Random Access Response contains instructions and parameters that determine the device's access rights and resource assignments, facilitating the reliable and orderly exchange of information between the device and the network.

Name: RAT
Definition: Radio Access Technology refers to the specific technology used in telecommunications to establish wireless connectivity between a mobile device and a network. It defines the method by which data and voice signals are transmitted and received over the air interface between the mobile device and the base station.

Name: RAU
Definition: Routing Area Updating refers to the process in telecommunications where a mobile device updates its current location to the network's routing area. This allows the network to keep track of the device's location and ensures that incoming calls, messages, and data can be correctly routed to the device.

Name: RB
Definition: Radio Bearer in the context of Telecommunications refers to the wireless communication channel between a mobile device and the network. It is responsible for carrying voice and data traffic between the mobile device and the network infrastructure. The radio bearer ensures the reliable and efficient transmission of information over the wireless link.

Name: RBAC
Definition: Role-Based Access Control is a method of regulating access to computer or network resources based on the roles of individual users within an organization. It is a widely used access control mechanism that helps ensure that users can only access the information and resources necessary for their job functions, thereby enhancing security and compliance

Name: RbD
Definition: Reliability by design review where all new products must go through it before they can launch.

Name: RCA
Definition: Root Cause Analysis in the context of Telecommunications refers to the systematic process of identifying and determining the underlying cause of a problem or issue occurring within the telecommunications network or system. This analysis aims to uncover the fundamental reason behind a particular incident, fault, or failure, enabling the telecommunications industry to address and resolve the root cause, rather than just treating the symptoms.

Name: RCC
Definition: Radio Frequency Color Code in the context of Telecommunications refers to a standardized color coding system that is used to identify specific radio frequency bands or channels.

Name: RCID
Definition: A number that Exclusive Partner Program assigns to eligible organizations. Example: Government of Canada has an RCID as an identifier.

Name: RCMS
Definition: Reward Customer Management System refers to a system used in customer service to manage and track rewards and incentives offered to customers. This system helps businesses keep track of customer loyalty programs, points accumulation, and redemptions. It streamlines the process of managing and administering rewards, making it easier for businesses to track and reward customer loyalty.

Name: RCP
Definition: Le rendement des capitaux propres est un indicateur qui mesure le rendement des capitaux propres du bilan qui est utilisé avec d’autres indicateurs financiers pour évaluer le rendement d’une entreprise. Pour calculer le RCP, on divise le bénéfice net par les capitaux propres. Le bénéfice net représente le profit total d’une entreprise après la déduction des dépenses et des taxes, tandis que les capitaux propres constituent la différence entre la valeur des actifs et des passifs d’une entreprise. Par exemple, imaginons qu’une entreprise possède un revenu annuel de deux millions de dollars et une moyenne de 15 millions de dollars en capitaux propres. Le RCP de l’entreprise est donc de 13 pour cent .

Name: RCT
Definition: Revenue Change per Transaction measures the difference in revenue generated per customer transaction over a specific time period. It helps evaluate whether your average earnings per sale are increasing or decreasing, indicating pricing trends, customer purchasing behavior, or product mix changes.

Name: RDA
Definition: Un ratio financier qui mesure la rentabilité d'une entreprise par rapport à ses actifs totaux. Il est calculé en divisant le bénéfice net par les actifs totaux.

Full Name: Reflective QoS flow to DRB mapping Indication
Name: RDI
Definition: Reflective QoS flow to DRB mapping Indication refers to a notification or signal in the field of telecommunications that identifies and establishes the mapping relationship between Reflective Quality of Service (QoS) flows and Dedicated Radio Bearers (DRBs). This indication is used to ensure efficient and effective communication between network entities by providing information on how Reflective QoS flows are associated with the appropriate DRBs.

Name: RDM
Definition: Processes that ensure that reference data is kept up to date and coordinated across an enterprise.

Name: RDS
Definition: Reliable Data Service in the context of Telecommunications refers to a consistent and dependable provision of data transmission and communication without disruptions or loss of information.

Name: RE
Definition: Routed Edge in the context of Telecommunications refers to the point in a network where traffic is directed and forwarded to its intended destination. It serves as a gateway or interface between the core network and the connected devices or endpoints. The Routed Edge efficiently routes data packets to ensure seamless communication between devices within the network.

Name: REC
Definition: A Renewable Energy Certificate is proof of the production of one megawatt-hour (MWh) of electricity generated from a renewable energy resource.

Name: RF
Definition: The definition of a rolling forecast is a report that uses historical data to predict future numbers continuously over a period of time. Rolling forecasts are often used in financial reporting, supply chain management, planning, and budgeting across every department.

Name: RFC
Definition: Request for Comments (RFC) is a formal process used to develop and propose standards, protocols, or procedures in various fields, including general technology. It allows individuals and organizations to openly review, discuss, and provide feedback on proposed ideas, specifications, or changes.

Name: RFI
Definition: A formal inquiry sent to suppliers to gather general information about their capabilities and offerings.

Name: RFP
Definition: A request for proposal is a document that solicits proposals, often made through a bidding or request process, by an agency or company interested in procurement of a commodity, service, or valuable asset, to potential suppliers to submit business proposals.

Name: RFQ
Definition: A formal document soliciting price quotes from suppliers for specific goods or services.

Name: RFS
Definition: Something (device, program, product) or someone (person) has been properly prepared and is now able to be used. Ready for Service is also a SAP Workflow name.

Name: RG
Definition: Residential Gateway is a device used in telecommunications that serves as a central connection point for various communication services within a home or residential area.

Name: RGU
Definition: An individual service subscriber who generates recurring revenue. For mobility: includes postpaid, prepaid and connected devices. For FFH: includes HSIA, TV, home phone and security subscribers. Also called “customer connections”

Name: RI
Definition: Rank Indicator in the context of telecommunications refers to a signal or code used to convey the hierarchical order or level of importance among users, devices, or connections within a communication system.

Name: RIE
Definition: Renewal in error is typically used to describe situations where a telecommunications service or contract is renewed incorrectly or unintentionally. Used to indicate that cancelling and reversing a renewal done in error; as if it never happened.

Name: RISE
Definition: The name of the unified retail and channel organization encompassing TELUS Stores, Mobile Klinik, and Channel People Development

Name: RIT
Definition: Radio Interface Technology refers to the technology used to establish and maintain wireless communication between a device and a network. It involves the protocols, standards, and techniques that enable the exchange of data and information over radio frequencies.

Name: RITM
Definition: le plus grand contrat avec le gouvernement du Quebec depuis 2008 qui est toujours valide à ce jour et encore pour quelques années(note de 2025). Quelques fois vous pourrez retrouver l'acronyme CTS-RITM ou CTS2-RITM. CTS fait référence à Contrat de Transition à la Sortie du RITM.

Name: RLC
Definition: Radio Link Control Protocol is a protocol used in telecommunications to ensure reliable transmission of data over radio links. It is responsible for managing the flow and error control of data between the transmitting and receiving devices.

Name: RLF
Definition: Radio Link Failure refers to a disruption or breakdown in the communication link between two radio devices in the field of telecommunications. It signifies a loss of signal or an inability to establish and maintain a reliable connection between the transmitting and receiving devices.

Name: RM
Definition: Reed-Muller refers to a mathematical representation used in telecommunications. It is a technique based on Boolean algebra and logic functions, which allows for the encoding and decoding of data. This method enables the efficient transmission and reception of digital information, ensuring reliable communication without the need for excessive error correction.

Name: RMA
Definition: Role at TELUS.

Name: RMMM
Definition: A risk management technique usually seen in the software Project plan.

Name: RMPU
Definition: Mesure des revenus par utilisateur ou abonné. Les valeurs RMPU présentées dans le rapport de surveillance des télécommunications se fondent sur les données mensuelles annuelles moyennes La source: Conseil de la radiodiffusion et des télécommunications canadiennes - Glossaire de télécommunications

Name: RMR
Definition: Recurring Monthly Revenue is the predictable total revenue generated by the business from all the active subscriptions in a particular month.

Name: RMSI
Definition: Remaining Minimum System Information refers to the essential data that is still required to be transmitted or received within a telecommunications system. It pertains to the necessary information that must be exchanged between devices or networks in order to ensure proper communication and functionality.

Name: RNTI
Definition: Radio Network Temporary Identifier (RNTI) is a unique identifier used in telecommunications to temporarily allocate resources within a radio network. It is a temporary identification value assigned to a user equipment (UE) or device in order to facilitate communication and enable efficient use of network resources. RNTI helps in distinguishing and managing different connections within a radio network, allowing for effective data transmission and control.

Name: RO
Definition: RACH Occasion in the context of Telecommunications refers to a specific time interval during which a mobile device can transmit a Random Access Channel (RACH) request to establish communication with the network.

Name: ROA
Definition: A financial ratio that measures a company's profitability relative to its total assets. It is calculated by dividing net income by total assets.

Name: ROC
Definition: All provinces except MB, SK, and QC.

Name: RoE
Definition: Is a metric that measures the return on balance sheet shareholders' equity and is used alongside other financial measures to assess a company's performance. The formula for calculating RoE is net income / shareholder equity. Net income represents the total profit a company earns after deducting all expenses and taxes, while shareholder equity is the difference between the company's assets and liabilities. For example, imagine a company with an annual income of $2M and average shareholders’ equity of $15M. This company’s ROE would be 13 per cent.

Name: RoHC
Definition: Robust Header Compression is a method used in telecommunications to efficiently compress the headers of data packets transmitted over a network.

Name: ROI
Definition: Return on Investment (ROI) is a financial performance measure used in finance and accounting to evaluate the profitability and effectiveness of an investment. It quantifies the return generated from an investment relative to its cost and is expressed as a percentage. ROI is calculated by dividing the net profit or gain from the investment by the initial cost of the investment, and then multiplying the result by 100. ROI provides a standardized way to assess the profitability of different investments and helps businesses and investors make informed decisions regarding the allocation of their resources.

Name: RPA
Definition: Robotic process automation is a form of business process automation technology based on metaphorical software robots or on artificial intelligence /digital workers.

Name: RPC
Definition: Changes to customer's monthly plan.

Name: RPM
Definition: TELUS coaching model used in the retail channel to support the needs of Team Members, Store Managers and Area Managers while taking care of TELUS Business and Customers. go/rpmperformance

Name: RPP
Definition: TELUS tool for tracking projects and resources. go/rpp

Name: RQI
Definition: Reflective QoS Attribute refers to a characteristic or parameter of Quality of Service (QoS) in telecommunications that relates to the ability of a network or service to assess and provide feedback on its own performance. It involves the capability of a system to monitor and evaluate various parameters of its own QoS, such as latency, packet loss, bandwidth, and jitter, in order to ensure the desired level of service is being maintained.

Name: RQoS
Definition: Reflective QoS in the context of telecommunications refers to the capability of a system to monitor and analyze its own network performance and adjust its Quality of Service (QoS) parameters accordingly. This enables the system to dynamically adapt and optimize its resource allocation in real-time based on the observed network conditions.

Name: RRA
Definition: Rapid Risk Assessment in the context of Enterprise refers to the quick evaluation and analysis of potential risks that a business or organization may face. It involves identifying and evaluating potential threats and vulnerabilities to the enterprise's assets, operations, and reputation. This assessment helps in making informed decisions to mitigate and manage risks effectively.

Name: RRC
Definition: Radio Resource Control Protocol is a protocol used in telecommunications that manages the allocation and control of radio resources between a mobile device and a base station.

Name: RRS
Definition: Team for outbound sales that was formed in response to COVID-19

Name: RRSP
Definition: Registered Retirement Savings Plan is a savings plan registered with the Canadian government to help individuals save for their retirement. Contributions to it are tax-deductible, and investment income earned within the plan is generally tax-sheltered until it is withdrawn, at which point it is taxed as income. Name: SOC 1
Definition: Service Organization Control 1 is one of audit report types within Service Organization Control standard. SOC1 is designed to evaluate the internal controls of a service organization that are relevant to the financial reporting of its user entities. Developed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA), SOC 1 reports are particularly important for organizations that provide services which could impact their clients' financial statements. Key aspects of Service Organization Control 1 Report: Purpose : The primary purpose of a SOC 1 report is to provide assurance to the user entities (clients) and their auditors that the service organization's controls are suitably designed and operating effectively to ensure accurate financial reporting. Audience : SOC 1 reports are intended for the management of the service organization, user entities, and the auditors of the user entities. They are not typically distributed to the general public. Criteria : The controls evaluated in a SOC 1 audit are based on the service organization's ability to meet the control objectives that are relevant to the user entities' financial reporting. Types of SOC 1 Reports : Type I : This report describes the service organization's system and the suitability of the design of controls at a specific point in time. It provides assurance that the controls are appropriately designed to achieve the control objectives. Type II : This report includes everything in a Type I report, plus it provides assurance on the operating effectiveness of those controls over a specified period of time (usually a minimum of six months). It demonstrates that the controls not only are suitably designed but also function effectively over time.

Name: SOC 2
Definition: Service Organization Control 2 is one of audit report types within Service Organization Control standard. SOC 2 is designed to evaluate the internal controls of a service organization related to information security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy. Developed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA), SOC 2 reports are particularly relevant for technology and cloud computing companies that handle customer data. Key aspects of Service Organization Control 2 report: Purpose : The primary purpose of a SOC 2 report is to provide assurance to customers and stakeholders that a service organization has implemented effective controls to protect their data and ensure the reliability of their services. Audience : SOC 2 reports are intended for a broad audience, including management, customers, regulators, and other stakeholders who need assurance about the service organization's controls related to data protection and operational effectiveness. Trust Service Criteria : SOC 2 reports are based on the AICPA’s Trust Service Criteria, which include: Security : The system is protected against unauthorized access (both physical and logical). Availability : The system is available for operation and use as committed or agreed. Processing Integrity : System processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized. Confidentiality : Information designated as confidential is protected as committed or agreed. Privacy : Personal information is collected, used, retained, disclosed, and disposed of in conformity with the commitments in the entity’s privacy notice. Types of SOC 2 Reports : Type I : This report describes the service organization's system and the suitability of the design of controls at a specific point in time. It provides assurance that the controls are appropriately designed to meet the trust service criteria. Type II : This report includes everything in a Type I report, plus it provides assurance on the operating effectiveness of those controls over a specified period of time (usually a minimum of six months). It demonstrates that the controls not only are suitably designed but also function effectively over time.

Name: SOC 3
Definition: Service Organization Control 3 is one of audit report types within Service Organization Control standard. SOC 3 is designed to provide assurance about the controls at a service organization related to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy. Like SOC 2, SOC 3 reports are based on the AICPA’s Trust Service Criteria. However, SOC 3 reports are intended for a general audience and provide a high-level summary of the service organization's controls without the detailed description and testing results found in SOC 2 reports. Key aspects of Service Organization Control 3 report: Purpose : The primary purpose of a SOC 3 report is to provide assurance to a broad audience, including customers, stakeholders, and the general public, that a service organization has effective controls in place to protect data and ensure the reliability of their services. Audience : SOC 3 reports are designed for a general audience and can be freely distributed. They are suitable for marketing purposes and for providing assurance to customers and stakeholders who do not require the detailed information found in SOC 2 reports. Trust Service Criteria : SOC 3 reports are based on the same Trust Service Criteria as SOC 2 reports, which include: Security : The system is protected against unauthorized access (both physical and logical). Availability : The system is available for operation and use as committed or agreed. Processing Integrity : System processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized. Confidentiality : Information designated as confidential is protected as committed or agreed. Privacy : Personal information is collected, used, retained, disclosed, and disposed of in conformity with the commitments in the entity’s privacy notice. Report Content : SOC 3 reports provide a high-level summary of the service organization's controls and the auditor's opinion on the effectiveness of those controls. They do not include the detailed description of the system, control objectives, or testing results that are found in SOC 2 reports.
