Definition: Subscription Concealed Identifier refers to a unique identification number or code used in telecommunications to conceal and protect the personal information of subscribers. It is used to anonymize an individual's identity and prevent unauthorized access to their personal data in communication services.

Name: SUL
Definition: Supplementary/Supplemental Uplink in the context of telecommunications refers to an additional transmission link or channel that is used to enhance the uplink capacity or data transfer capabilities of a communication system.

Name: SUPI
Definition: Subscription Permanent Identifier refers to a unique code or number assigned to a telecommunications subscription that serves as a permanent identification for the subscriber.

Name: SVOC
Definition: A Single View Of Customer, also known as "360-degree view of customer" or "unified customer view"; is a comprehensive, centralized representation of all customer data and interactions across various touchpoints and systems within an organization.

Name: SVOD
Definition: Subscription Video On Demand refers to a service provided to customers that allows them to access a library of video content for a recurring fee. This type of service enables customers to stream or download videos on demand, giving them the flexibility to watch content at their own convenience.

Name: SWS
Definition: SmartWear Security is a line of wearable accessories in the form of jewellery and key charms which connect users to the emergency support and 24/7 monitoring.

Name: SWT
Definition: Standardized Work Time refers to a predetermined and consistent amount of time allocated for performing tasks within an enterprise. It involves establishing fixed durations for completing specific activities, ensuring that all employees follow the same time standards for carrying out their work.

Name: T.Tech
Definition: TELUS technology solutions includes network revenues and equipment sales arising from mobile technologies, data revenues, healthcare software and technology solutions, voice and other telecommunications services revenues, and equipment sales.

Name: T2B
Definition: Call Centre metric. Percentage of 4 and 5 scores obtained in customer satisfaction survey assessing customer's perception of the agent's performance. 4 being Very good and 5 being Excellent.

Name: TA
Definition: Timing Advance is a parameter in telecommunications that denotes the adjustment made to the transmission timing of a mobile device in relation to the base station.

Name: TACG
Definition: TELUS Agriculture & Consumer Goods refers to the application of telecommunications and information technology in the agricultural sector. This involves using advanced technologies to gather data, analyze it, and provide insights to improve efficiency, productivity, and profitability in the agriculture and consumer goods industries.

Name: TAT
Definition: Turn Around Time refers to the duration required to complete a task or process in a general context.

Name: TAU
Definition: Tracking Area Updating is the process in telecommunications where a mobile device informs the network about its updated location in order to maintain uninterrupted connectivity.

Name: TB
Definition: Terabyte is a unit of digital information in the field of telecommunications, representing approximately one trillion bytes of data.

Name: TBC
Definition: To Be Clarified in the context of General means that there is a lack of information or understanding about a particular subject or topic. It indicates that further explanation or clarification is required to fully comprehend and address the issue at hand.

Name: TBO
Definition: Change in ownership or partnership.

Name: TBS
Definition: TELUS Business Solutions in the context of Enterprise refers to the range of products and services that TELUS provides to meet the specific needs and requirements of businesses.

Full Name: TELUS Business Solutions Change Management Centre of Excellence
Name: TBS CM CoE
Definition: TELUS team name

Name: TC4G
Definition: TELUS Change for Good is TELUS' bill round-up program that enables consumer mobility and home services customers to round-up their bills to the next dollar and 100% of the round-up value goes to TELUS Friendly Future Foundation. Program page: telus.com/changeforgood The 'TELUS' is part of the program name and always has to be legally. Program was initially called Donate the Change from December 2019 to March 2022.

Name: TCC
Definition: TELUS Command Center is the team at TELUS Incident management team . Find out more on Habitat

Name: TCCE
Definition: TELUS Cloud Collaboration Enterprise refers to a cloud-based collaboration solution designed specifically for businesses. It allows enterprises to enhance their communication and collaboration capabilities by leveraging cloud technology.

Name: TCH
Definition: Traffic Channel refers to a designated portion of a telecommunications system that is used for transmitting voice or data signals between two or more communication endpoints. It is a communication pathway established within the system for the purpose of transmitting user information.

Name: TCI
Definition: TELUS Communications Inc. is an enterprise that provides communication services to businesses.

Name: TCO
Definition: Total Cost of Ownership refers to the overall expense associated with acquiring, owning, and maintaining an asset or investment, taking into account all direct and indirect costs incurred. This concept is an important metric for finance and accounting as it provides a comprehensive evaluation of expenses beyond the initial purchase price, enabling a more accurate assessment of the true cost of an asset over its entire lifecycle.

Name: TCP
Definition: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is a fundamental protocol in telecommunications. It is a reliable, connection-oriented protocol that enables the transmission of data over networks. TCP ensures that data is transmitted in an ordered and error-free manner by dividing it into packets and establishing a virtual connection between the sender and receiver. This protocol guarantees the successful delivery of data, making it a critical component in the reliable exchange of information over networks.

Name: TCS
Definition: TELUS Customer Solutions refers to the range of services and support provided by TELUS, a telecommunications company, to assist and address the needs of its customers. It includes various solutions and assistance provided to customers, such as troubleshooting technical issues, resolving billing inquiries, guiding customers on using different telecommunications services, and offering personalized solutions to meet their individual requirements.

Name: TCSS
Definition: TELUS application

Name: TCTS
Definition: A company that provides business transformation, managed network operations, network outsourcing, and consultancy services to telecommunication companies around the world

Name: TD
Definition: TELUS Digital is a division of TELUS. It operates under the full name Telus International (Cda) Inc. and it trades on stock exchanges under the ticker symbol TIXT

Name: TDD
Definition: Time Division Duplex refers to a telecommunications technique that allows for simultaneous transmission and reception of data within a given frequency band. It involves dividing the available time into alternating time slots for both transmitting and receiving data, thereby enabling bidirectional communication.

Name: TDF
Definition: Traffic Detection Function is a feature or capability within telecommunications systems that is responsible for identifying and categorizing different types of network traffic. It is specifically designed to analyze and recognize various protocols and applications used in network communications. By accurately detecting and classifying traffic, this function helps in effectively managing and controlling network resources, optimizing data flow, and enabling efficient network operations.

Name: TDIM
Definition: TELUS Digital Incident Management in the context of Enterprise refers to the process and systems in place to handle and resolve incidents that occur within TELUS digital services or platforms. It involves a systematic approach of identifying, reporting, and addressing any disruptions or issues that may arise, with the goal of minimizing impact on business operations and ensuring quick resolution.

Name: TDL
Definition: A Technical Debt Ledger is a tool or document used to track and manage technical debt within a software development project or organization. Technical debt refers to the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy (limited) solution now instead of using a better approach that would take longer. The ledger helps teams keep a record of these "debts" so they can be addressed systematically over time. The Technical Debt Ledger at TELUS allows any team member to log a known customer reliability risk via the Submit Technical Debt button at go/reliability . Since its launch in 2021, it has become the de facto repository for all known reliability risks across TELUS and its used to process risk entries, identify some existing risk without manual input, more accurately measure risk while improving governance, analysis and reporting.

Name: TDMA
Definition: Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) is a telecommunications technique that enables multiple users to share the same frequency channel by dividing it into different time slots. Each user is assigned a specific time slot during which they can transmit and receive data or voice signals. This method optimizes the utilization of the available bandwidth by allowing multiple users to access the channel sequentially rather than simultaneously.

Name: TDOG
Definition: TELUS Day of Giving is an annual event in the field of telecommunications where TELUS, a telecommunications company, organizes a dedicated day for employees to participate in various community service activities. This initiative showcases TELUS' commitment to giving back to society by engaging its employees in volunteer work and supporting local communities.

Name: TDS
Definition: Individuals who have operational level responsibility for data capture, maintenance and delivery. They are appointed to take on a leadership role for implementing necessary processes, solutions and technology which supports business goals, operational efficiency , data ethics, trust and governance; responsible for day to day maintenance of data; Recommending appropriate procedures that satisfy specified data and information requirements; Implementing necessary processes and solutions. A Technical Data Steward supports their Business Data Steward counterpart in order to create and support the processes that would allow the establishment of creating defined data process needs that support business goals

Name: TDWI
Definition: A leading provider of education and research in business intelligence and data warehousing.

Name: TEFD
Definition: Technology Enablement Front Door in the context of Telecommunications refers to a system or mechanism that provides a centralized and streamlined approach for integrating and implementing technology solutions in the telecommunications industry. It acts as a gateway or entry point to enable the adoption and utilization of various technological advancements and innovations within the telecommunications infrastructure.

Name: TEID
Definition: Tunnel Endpoint ID is an identifier used in telecommunications to identify the endpoint of a tunnel.

Name: TEM
Definition: TELUS Expert Messaging in the context of Enterprise refers to a communication service provided by TELUS specifically designed for businesses. It enables enterprises to communicate with experts and professionals through messaging channels, facilitating efficient and direct interactions for the purpose of seeking information, guidance, or support.

Name: TES
Definition: Team name.

Name: TFD
Definition: Customer discount for having multiple lines on their account.

Name: TFSA
Definition: Tax-Free Savings Account is a savings account offered by financial institutions in Canada. This type of account allows Canadians to save money without having to pay tax on the interest earned or on withdrawals made from the account. The contributions are not tax-deductible, but any money earned in the account, including interest, dividends and capital gains, are tax-free. This makes it an attractive option for Canadians looking to save for short-term or long-term financial goals.

Name: THCC
Definition: TELUS Health Care Centres are medical facilities located across Canada that provide various healthcare services. Link to resource site: https://sites.google.com/telus.com/carecentreshub/home

Name: THCP
Definition: TELUS Health Cloud Platform is a digital infrastructure designed specifically for the healthcare industry. It is a secure and scalable platform that allows healthcare organizations to securely store, manage, and access patient health data and other relevant information in a cloud-based environment. The platform enables healthcare professionals to collaborate, share data, and access information in a streamlined and efficient manner, ultimately improving the delivery of healthcare services.

Name: THFS
Definition: TELUS Heath & Financial Services refers to a range of healthcare services and financial solutions offered by TELUS to support individuals and organizations in the healthcare industry. These services are designed to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and effectiveness of healthcare delivery and management. They may include software platforms, data analytics, communication tools, and financial solutions tailored to the specific needs of healthcare providers, insurers, and patients. The aim is to enhance patient care, streamline processes, and facilitate better financial management within the healthcare sector.

Name: THPS
Definition: TELUS Health and Payment Solutions refers to a division within the enterprise that focuses on providing healthcare-related technology solutions and payment processing services.

Name: THS
Definition: TELUS Health Solutions is a healthcare company that provides comprehensive solutions for the healthcare industry.

Name: THX
Definition: TELUS Health Exchange refers to a healthcare platform that facilitates the secure and efficient exchange of medical information among healthcare providers, patients, and other relevant stakeholders. It enables the seamless sharing of patient records, clinical data, and other health-related information in order to improve care coordination, enhance patient outcomes, and streamline healthcare processes.

Name: THX-i
Definition: TELUS Health Exchange International is a platform that enables the exchange of health-related information and data on an international scale within the healthcare industry. It facilitates the secure and seamless transfer of patient records, test results, and other relevant medical information between healthcare providers, organizations, and systems across different countries. This exchange of information aims to enhance collaboration and coordination among healthcare professionals globally, ultimately leading to improved healthcare outcomes for patients.

Name: TI
Definition: TELUS International is a branch of TELUS specifically focused on providing telecommunications services on an international scale.

Name: TINAA
Definition: TELUS Intelligence Analytics and Automation in the context of Enterprise refers to the utilization of advanced data analysis techniques and automated processes to gain valuable insights and streamline operational activities within an organization.

Name: TLC
Definition: Termination Liability Charge refers to the financial obligation a company incurs when terminating a contract or agreement before its fulfillment. It is a charge on the company's balance sheet that represents the estimated costs associated with the early termination, including penalties, legal fees, and other related expenses. This charge reflects the potential financial impact of ending a contractual commitment prematurely.

Name: TLP
Definition: TELUS Leadership Philosophy in the context of telecommunications refers to the guiding principles and values that TELUS, a telecommunications company, follows in order to lead and manage their organization effectively. It encompasses the beliefs and practices that shape the way TELUS leaders operate and make decisions to achieve their goals and objectives. It sets the standard for leadership behaviors, communication, employee development, and the overall culture within the company.

Name: TLS
Definition: Transport Layer Security is a protocol that provides secure communication between network applications by encrypting the data transmitted over a network, ensuring confidentiality and integrity.

Name: TM
Definition: TELUS Mobility in the context of Enterprise refers to a mobile telecommunications service provided by TELUS specifically designed for businesses and organizations.

Name: TMM
Definition: TELUS Market Model is a framework or strategy used in the telecommunications industry to analyze and understand market conditions, dynamics, and trends. It involves studying various factors such as customer needs, competition, technology advancements, and regulatory environment to develop effective business plans and make informed decisions. The model helps telecommunications companies like TELUS to assess market demand, identify target segments, determine pricing strategies, and allocate resources efficiently. By understanding the market model, companies can stay competitive, drive growth, and adapt to changing market conditions effectively.

Name: TMODS
Definition: The name of TELUS database resource.

Name: TMSC
Definition: TELUS Material Support Centre is a dedicated team operating within the TELUS Digital organization, responsible for delivering specialized SAP material management support and technical expertise to multiple business areas throughout the TELUS enterprise.

Name: TMSI
Definition: Temporary Mobile Subscriber Identity (TMSI) refers to a unique identification number assigned to a mobile device within a cellular network for a limited period of time. It is used to maintain user privacy and prevent unauthorized access to sensitive information.

Name: TN
Definition: Timeslot Number is a numerical identifier used in telecommunications to uniquely identify a specific time interval within a communication channel or system. It is used to divide the available time into discrete units, allowing multiple users or signals to share the same resources efficiently.

Name: TNIS
Definition: A joint standards committee at TELUS that leads innovation through a single, unified, and integrated vision for network standards. Committee's internal page

Name: TOCS
Definition: Team Operational Cost to Serve is a performance metric that measures the total costs associated with a team delivering its services or products to customers.

Name: TOM
Definition: An internal platform used to create, manage, and publish product and service offers to the market.

Name: TOS
Definition: TELUS Online Security plans Powered by NortonLifeLockTM.

Name: TOWN
Definition: Transfer Of Ownership refers to the legal process by which the rights, responsibilities, and control over a property, asset, or entity are transferred from one party to another, typically through a legally binding agreement or transaction.

Name: TPIA
Definition: Third-party Internet access services are wholesale high-speed access services of large cable carriers that enable independent service providers to offer retail Internet services to their own end-users. As a result of the availability of TPIA services, residential and business end-users have greater choice in the Internet services that are available to them. TPIA services are offered under terms and conditions that must be approved by the Commission, whereas the Commission has refrained from regulating the rates and most terms and conditions applicable to retail Internet service offerings. Sourced from Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission.

Name: TPM
Definition: Trusted Platform Module (TPM) is a hardware-based security feature used in telecommunications. It is designed to provide secure storage and cryptographic functions for sensitive data and ensure the integrity and security of a telecommunications platform. TPM helps protect against unauthorized access, tampering, and data breaches by providing a secure environment for cryptographic operations and storing encryption keys.

Name: TPS
Definition: Business unit/ department. Provides innovative and integrated solutions to national and global service providers looking for IP, data, bandwidth and voice services into and within Canada.

Name: TQ
Definition: Business unit/team name.

Name: TR
Definition: Technical Report in the context of General refers to a formal document that presents detailed information, analysis, and findings about a specific technical topic or project. It typically includes technical data, methodologies, results, and recommendations related to a scientific or engineering investigation.

Name: TR-COE
Definition: A Technical Resolution Center of Excellence is a specialized unit within an organization that focuses on providing high-quality technical support and problem resolution.

Name: TRG
Definition: TELUS Resource Groups are employee-led groups within TELUS that focus on fostering diversity, inclusion, and community engagement within the organization. These groups are designed to support employees from various backgrounds and identities, providing a platform for networking, professional development, and advocacy.

Name: TRL
Definition: Telus Retail Limited in the context of Enterprise refers to a company or division within Telus that focuses on retail operations. It typically involves the sale of Telus products and services to consumers through physical retail stores or online platforms.

Name: TRM
Definition: TELUS Risk Management in the context of Enterprise refers to a systematic approach aimed at identifying, assessing, and mitigating potential risks that may impact the operations, financial stability, and reputation of the organization. It involves the implementation of strategies and processes to proactively identify, analyze, and address any potential threats or uncertainties to successfully manage the risks faced by the enterprise.

Name: TRP
Definition: Transmission/Reception Point refers to a specific location within a telecommunications network where the transfer and receipt of data or information occurs.

Name: TRV
Definition: Name of a quality assurance program/tool.

Name: TS
Definition: Technical Specification in the context of General refers to a detailed document that outlines the technical requirements, features, and characteristics of a product, system, or process. It provides precise information about the design, functionality, performance, and other specifications necessary for the development, implementation, or evaluation of the subject matter.

Name: TSA
Definition: A type of an agreement that is made between the buyer and seller of a company. In this arrangement, the seller agrees to provide certain services to the buyer at a predetermined price.

Name: TSB
Definition: Security solutions for business customers

Name: TSBT
Definition: Business unit name

Name: TSC
Definition: Training Sequence Code in the context of Telecommunications refers to a specific code or pattern of bits used during the training phase of a communication system. It is used to help estimate channel characteristics, synchronize timing, and optimize system performance.

Name: TSDSI
Definition: Telecommunications Standards Development Society India is an organization that plays a significant role in the development and establishment of telecommunications standards in India.

Name: TSG
Definition: Technical Specification Group in the context of Telecommunications refers to a specialized working group within a telecommunications standards organization that is responsible for developing and defining technical specifications for various aspects of telecommunications technologies and systems.

Name: TSIRT
Definition: TELUS Security Incident Response Team is a specialized group within an enterprise that is responsible for promptly and effectively responding to and managing any security incidents that may occur. Their main objective is to detect, analyze, and mitigate any potential threats or breaches to the organization's information systems and network infrastructure. The team is equipped with the necessary knowledge, expertise, and tools to investigate and resolve security incidents, minimize damage, and restore normal operations as quickly as possible, ensuring the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of the organization's data and systems.

Name: TSM
Definition: Trusted service manager is an intermediary between the Mobile Network Operator and the Service Provider and provides the user with unique encryption data.

Name: TSN
Definition: The Sports Network in the context of Telecommunications refers to a media channel or platform that focuses specifically on the broadcasting and distribution of sports-related content.

Name: TSO
Definition: TELUS Strategy & Operations refers to the strategic planning and execution of operational processes within the telecommunications industry. It involves developing and implementing effective strategies to achieve business objectives, optimizing internal operations, and ensuring efficient delivery of telecommunications services to customers.

Name: TSR
Definition: Technical Support Representative in the context of Enterprise refers to an individual responsible for providing assistance and troubleshooting technical issues for customers or clients.

Name: TSSI
Definition: TELUS Sourcing Solutions Inc is a telecommunications company that specializes in providing sourcing solutions.

Name: TTA
Definition: Telecommunications Technology Association refers to an organization that focuses on the development and standardization of technologies related to telecommunications. It plays a crucial role in shaping the industry by establishing guidelines and protocols for various telecommunications systems and services.

Name: TTC
Definition: Telecommunication Technology Committee refers to a specific committee within the field of telecommunications that focuses on technological advancements, developments, and standards in telecommunication systems and networks. This committee plays a crucial role in analyzing and determining the best technical practices, protocols, and guidelines for telecommunications technologies.

Name: TTI
Definition: Transmission Time Interval (TTI) refers to the specific time duration allocated for transmitting a unit of data within a telecommunications system. It is a fixed interval of time within which data packets, frames, or symbols are sent from the transmitter to the receiver. The TTI is a crucial parameter that determines the efficiency and reliability of data transmission in various telecommunications technologies.

Name: TTM
Definition: Trailing Twelve Month refers to a period of time consisting of the last 12 consecutive months, typically used in finance and accounting to assess performance or analyze financial data. It provides a snapshot of the past year's financial results, allowing for better trend analysis and comparison against previous periods.

Name: TTV
Definition: TELUS Television services (Optik TV, Pik TV & Satellite TV)

Name: TVS
Definition: TELUS Visual Support is a specialized application that is designed to aid network diagnostics and WiFi troubleshooting. TELUS Visual Support application is developed by RouteThis company, this application aims to enhance customer and agent experience.

Name: TWA
Definition: A discounted mobile phone plan that TELUS employees have access to.

Name: TWAG
Definition: Trusted Wireless Access Gateway refers to a telecommunications device or system that securely connects wireless devices to a network or the internet. It provides a secure and reliable method for wireless devices to access and communicate with the network, ensuring data protection and access control.

Name: TWHI
Definition: TELUS Wireless Home Internet is a fixed wireless broadband service that provides high-speed internet to homes using TELUS's 5G and LTE wireless networks.

Name: TWHID
Definition: TELUS Wireless Home Internet Device is the physical hardware equipment that enables the wireless home internet service.

Name: TX
Definition: Transmitter Exchange refers to the process in telecommunications where the transmission equipment is replaced or interchanged. This involves swapping or upgrading the transmitters used in a network or communication system.

Name: TXRU
Definition: Transmitter Receiver Unit, in the context of Telecommunications, refers to a device or module that combines the functions of both a transmitter and a receiver. It is responsible for transmitting and receiving signals in a telecommunications system without the need for separate components.

Name: UAR
Definition: A periodic audit process to verify that user access rights remain appropriate and compliant.

Name: UAT
Definition: User Acceptance Testing is a process in which real end-users evaluate a system or software to ensure that it meets their requirements and functions as expected.

Name: UBB
Definition: Usage-Based Billing in the context of Telecommunications refers to a billing method that charges customers based on the amount of specific service they use, rather than a fixed monthly fee or a flat rate.

Name: UC
Definition: A use case is a description of how a person who uses that process or system will accomplish a goal.

Name: UCI
Definition: Uplink Control Information refers to the data transmitted from a terminal device to a base station in telecommunications. It comprises essential control information that is necessary for establishing and maintaining the communication link between the terminal and the base station.

Name: UDE
Definition: Unix Desktop Environment refers to a graphical user interface (GUI) provided by Unix-like operating systems for users to interact with the system.

Name: UDM
Definition: Unified Data Management in the context of Telecommunications refers to the comprehensive and centralized management of data across different systems and networks within the telecommunications industry. It involves the integration, organization, and control of various types of data, such as customer information, network performance data, billing data, and service provisioning data. The purpose of Unified Data Management is to ensure consistency, accuracy, and accessibility of data, enabling efficient operations, effective decision-making, and seamless customer experiences.

Name: UDP
Definition: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is a network protocol used in telecommunications to facilitate the transmission of data between devices in an IP network. It is a connectionless protocol that works on the transport layer of the Internet Protocol Suite. UDP provides a simple and efficient method for sending datagrams, or discrete units of data, without establishing a dedicated communication channel or ensuring reliable delivery. Unlike other protocols, UDP does not provide error checking or retransmission mechanisms, making it suitable for real-time applications where speed is crucial, but reliability can be sacrificed.

Name: UDR
Definition: Unified Data Repository refers to a central storage system in the field of telecommunications that securely consolidates and organizes diverse data sources, such as customer information, network data, and operational data. It serves as a comprehensive repository where different types of data can be stored, managed, and accessed by various systems and applications within a telecom network.

Name: UDS
Definition: A shared set of design standards, components, and guidelines used to ensure consistent user experiences.

Name: UDSF
Definition: Unstructured Data Storage Function refers to a storage system within the telecommunications industry that is designed to handle data that doesn't have a predefined structure or format. This function enables telecom companies to store and manage vast amounts of diverse data, such as text documents, videos, images, and other unstructured information. The primary purpose of this function is to provide efficient storage and retrieval capabilities for unstructured data, regardless of its format or size.

Name: UE
Definition: User Equipment refers to the equipment or devices used by end-users in the field of telecommunications. It includes devices such as mobile phones, tablets, laptops, and other portable devices that connect to wireless networks to access voice, data, and multimedia services.

Name: UFMC
Definition: Universally Filtered Multicarrier refers to a telecommunications technique that involves the use of multiple carrier signals to transmit data, while also incorporating universally filtered modulation. This approach combines multiple carriers and applies a filtering process to ensure optimum signal quality and efficiency. This technique allows for improved performance and enhanced spectral efficiency in the transmission of data over a communication channel.

Name: UGR
Definition: Abonné à un service individuel qui génère des revenus récurrents. Pour les services mobiles, cela inclut les services postpayé et prépayé, ainsi que les appareils connectés. Pour les services filaires, cela inclut l’accès Internet haute vitesse, le service de télévision, le service de téléphonie à domicile et les services de sécurité. Aussi appelées « connexions clients ».

Name: UHD
Definition: Ultra High Definition in the context of telecommunications refers to a technology that provides an extremely high level of visual detail and clarity in images and videos.

Name: UICC
Definition: Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) is a term commonly used in the telecommunications industry. It refers to a smart card that securely stores and processes data for mobile telecommunications devices. UICCs are typically used in mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets to store SIM (Subscriber Identity Module) cards, which are required for authentication and identification purposes on cellular networks. These cards contain integrated circuits that enable them to securely store personal information and perform cryptographic functions necessary for secure communication with the network. UICCs play a crucial role in enabling mobile devices to connect to and communicate with cellular networks, ensuring the secure transmission of data and enabling various telecommunications services, such as voice calls, messaging, and mobile internet access.

Name: UL
Definition: Uplink refers to the transmission path that carries data from a user device or a lower-level network to a higher-level network or satellite. It is a method used in telecommunications to transfer information in an upward direction, typically from a user or client device to a central or remote server.

Name: ULCL
Definition: Uplink Classifier refers to a component or feature in telecommunications that identifies and categorizes incoming data or signals transmitted from a user or device to the network. It is responsible for analyzing the characteristics of the data and determining how it should be treated or prioritized within the network infrastructure.

Name: UM
Definition: Unacknowledged Mode in the context of telecommunications refers to a communication channel or protocol where the receiving device does not send any acknowledgment or confirmation to the sender to indicate successful reception of the transmitted data.

Name: Uma
Definition: Urban Macro in the context of Telecommunications refers to a type of cellular network infrastructure that consists of large, powerful base stations strategically placed in urban areas to provide extensive coverage and handle high-capacity data traffic without the need for frequent handoffs between cells.

Name: Umbi
Definition: Urban Micro in the context of telecommunications refers to small-scale cellular network infrastructure designed to provide coverage and capacity in densely populated urban areas.

Name: UMTS
Definition: Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS) is a wireless communication technology that provides high-speed data and voice services. It is a third-generation (3G) mobile system that uses a combination of wideband code division multiple access (WCDMA) and time division duplexing (TDD) techniques to support various mobile applications and services. UMTS offers enhanced data transfer rates and improved network capacity compared to its predecessors, enabling users to access the internet, make video calls, send multimedia messages, and engage in other advanced mobile communications.

Name: UOST
Definition: Universal Order Status Tracker is an order tracking and status management platform that assists customer service agents in real-time tracking and determining comprehensive order details across wireline subscription services, providing unified visibility into order status, progress, and fulfillment information.

Name: UP
Definition: User Plane in the context of Telecommunications refers to the part of the network that is responsible for transmitting user data.

Name: UPC
Definition: A centralized repository of all products and services offered, with consistent attributes and descriptions.

Name: UPF
Definition: User Plane Function in the context of Telecommunications refers to the part of a network that handles the transmission and routing of user data. It is responsible for the efficient transfer of information between different devices and applications without any delay or interruption.

Name: UPOB
Definition: The remaining portion of a contractual commitment to deliver goods or services not yet completed.

Name: URI
Definition: Universal Resource Identifier is a standardized method of identifying resources in the field of telecommunications. It is a string of characters used to uniquely identify a resource, such as a webpage or a file, on the internet.

Name: URLLC
Definition: Ultra-Reliable Low Latency Communication refers to a type of telecommunications technology that offers highly dependable and minimal delay data transmission.

Name: URN
Definition: Universal Resource Name in the context of telecommunications refers to a unique identifier that is used to identify and locate resources in a network without specifying the particular access method or location details.

Name: USF
Definition: Uplink State Flag refers to a specific signal indicator used in telecommunications systems. This flag is utilized to indicate the state or status of the uplink channel, which is the data transmission path from a user device to a base station or satellite. The flag provides information on the condition and availability of the uplink channel, allowing the system to determine if it is ready to receive data or if there are any issues that need to be addressed.

Name: USIM
Definition: Universal Subscriber Identity Module (USIM) is a type of smart card used in telecommunications that securely stores and manages subscriber identities in mobile devices. It provides authentication and encryption functionalities, allowing subscribers to access and utilize various mobile services, such as voice calls, messaging, and data transfer, on a mobile network. The USIM card contains unique identification information and security keys, enabling secure communication between the mobile device and the network infrastructure.

Name: UTRAN
Definition: Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network, in the context of Telecommunications, is a network architecture that provides wireless connectivity between user equipment (UE) and the core network. It enables the transmission of voice, data, and multimedia services over a terrestrial radio interface, offering wide coverage and high-quality performance.

Name: V2I
Definition: Vehicle-to-Infrastructure refers to a telecommunications concept where vehicles are able to communicate and exchange information with the infrastructure around them, such as traffic signals, road sensors, and transportation management systems.

Name: V2N
Definition: Vehicle-to-Network refers to the communication exchange between vehicles and a telecommunication network.

Name: V2V
Definition: Vehicle-to-Vehicle in the context of Telecommunications refers to a communication system that enables direct communication between two or more motor vehicles.

Name: V2X
Definition: Vehicle-to-X is a telecommunications concept that refers to the exchange of information between vehicles and other entities, such as roadside infrastructure, pedestrians, or other vehicles.

Full Name: Voice services over Adaptive Multi-user channels on One Slot
Name: VAMOS
Definition: Voice services over Adaptive Multi-user channels on One Slot refers to a telecommunications technology that allows multiple users to transmit and receive voice signals over a single time slot. This method optimizes the efficiency and capacity of the communication system by dynamically allocating resources among multiple users in a flexible and adaptive manner. It enables efficient utilization of network resources, improving overall voice communication quality and increasing the number of concurrent voice calls that can be accommodated within a given bandwidth.

Name: VAR
Definition: Verbatim analysis is the process of quantifying feedback from survey respondents. Link to form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScygNhMoCoPxFgibq9jH6rGNbINV6PpuPoAEPEUHJR_6R2XFw/viewform

Name: VBA
Definition: A Microsoft programming language used to automate tasks and build custom functions within Excel.

Name: VC
Definition: The Voice core distribution/aggregation layer is dedicated for voice over internet protocol service that at one end connects to Nortel Packet Voice Gateways using Gigabit Ethernet and to Communication Server 2000 using Gigabit Ethernet on the other end.

Name: VCC
Definition: Voice Call Continuity refers to the seamless transition of an ongoing voice call from one network to another, ensuring uninterrupted communication for the participants.

Name: VCT
Definition: A software-based point-of-sale system enabling electronic payment processing without physical hardware.

Name: VDI
Definition: TELUS Application

Name: VDSL
Definition: Very-high-bit-rate Digital Subscriber Line (VDSL) is a type of telecommunications technology that allows for high-speed internet access over existing copper telephone lines.

Name: VFS
Definition: Value for Signal. differs slightly from the older FFC (Fee for Carriage) term. The concept is the ability of OTA services to charge (or negotiate) a fee for BDUs to carry their signal. It was seen as a way to financially support OTA but died away when the BDUs bought OTAs and the Supreme Court of Canada decided that the CRTC did not have jurisdiction to impose a VFS regulatory framework.

Name: VI
Definition: Vertical Integration or Vertically Integrated refers to cable or satellite companies which own broadcasters which in some cases also own production companies. The CRTC’s ‘VI Code’ governs the relationship between BDUs and independent broadcasters so that the independent broadcasters are protected from market dominance by the vertically integrated companies.

Name: VID
Definition: VLAN Identifier refers to a numerical tag that is assigned to a virtual local area network (VLAN) in the field of telecommunications.

Name: VLAN
Definition: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) refers to a network technology used in telecommunications that enables the creation of logical and isolated networks within a physical local area network (LAN).

Name: VLDB
Definition: Databases that pose unusual performance challenges due to their exceptional size.

Name: VNF
Definition: Virtual Network Function refers to a software component or service that replicates the functionality of traditional network hardware appliances. It is used in the field of telecommunications to enable the virtualization of network functions, such as routing, firewalling, or load balancing, on software-based platforms. By utilizing virtualization technologies, Virtual Network Functions can be deployed and managed more flexibly and efficiently, improving network scalability and reducing deployment costs.

Name: VOC
Definition: Voice of the Customer in the context of Customer Service refers to the feedback, opinions, and preferences expressed by customers regarding their experiences with a product or service.

Name: VOD
Definition: Video On Demand in the context of Telecommunications refers to a service that allows users to access and watch desired video content at their convenience, without having to adhere to a predetermined schedule.

Name: VoIP
Definition: A service or capability utilizing both hardware and software that enables users to employ IP networks, such as the Internet, as the transmission medium for voice communication

Name: VoLTE
Definition: Voice over LTE (VoLTE) is a communication technology that enables voice calls to be made over a 4G LTE network. It uses the internet protocol (IP) to transmit voice data packets, allowing for high-quality voice calls to be made and received using LTE networks. VoLTE offers a more efficient use of network resources and provides better call quality compared to traditional circuit-switched voice calls.

Name: VoNR
Definition: Voice over New Radio (VoNR) refers to a technology that enables voice communication over the New Radio (NR) protocol, which is a part of the 5th Generation (5G) telecommunications network. It allows voice calls to be transmitted using the NR air interface, providing a high-quality, low-latency, and efficient voice communication service. VoNR eliminates the need for legacy voice networks, such as 2G or 3G, and enables voice calls to be seamlessly integrated into the 5G network architecture.

Name: VOW
Definition: Voice over Wireless is a wireless network process for voice communication over a wireless local area network . It enables voice or audio communication on a typical wireless network through Wi-Fi or wireless, voice-enabled devices.

Name: VoWiFi
Definition: Voice Over WiFi refers to the technology that allows voice calls to be transmitted over a WiFi network instead of traditional cellular networks.

Name: VPLMN
Definition: Visited PLMN refers to a Mobile Network Operator (MNO) that a subscriber is currently connected to while roaming outside their home network.

Name: VPN
Definition: A Virtual Private Network is a technology that creates a secure and encrypted connection over a less secure network, such as the internet. It allows users to securely access and transmit data over public networks as if their devices were directly connected to a private network. VPNs are commonly used to protect sensitive data, maintain privacy, bypass geo-restrictions, and enhance security when accessing the internet. VPNs can be used for personal privacy and security, as well as for business purposes to secure remote connections and protect confidential information. Virtual Private Network extends a private network over a public network, or in other words an Intranet over the Internet.

Full Name: Virtual Point of Presence (last mile DSL network for business)
Name: VPOP
Definition: Virtual Point of Presence (last mile DSL network for business) refers to a virtual network infrastructure that enables businesses to connect to the internet through DSL technology. It serves as the final link between the internet service provider's network and the customer's premises. This virtual point of presence allows businesses to access high-speed DSL connections, facilitating reliable and efficient internet connectivity without the need for physical equipment or infrastructure specific to each customer.

Name: VPP
Definition: Virtual Power Plant are networks of small energy-producing or storage devices, like solar panels and batteries, that are pooled together to serve the electricity grid.

Name: VQX
Definition: Statistical measure of the video quality of a television subscriber.

Name: VR
Definition: Virtual Reality refers to the experience of being immersed in a computer-simulated environment, where users can interact with and explore a three-dimensional world.

Name: VRS
Definition: Video Relay Service is a telecommunications feature that allows individuals who use sign language to communicate with others over video calls. It enables a sign language user to make a phone call through a relay operator who then translates the call between sign language and spoken language in real time. This service facilitates effective communication between individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing and those who can hear, bridging the gap between different forms of communication.

Name: VSIT
Definition: Link: https://sites.google.com/telus.com/welcomevsit

Name: VSOS
Definition: Voluntary Suspension of Service in the context of telecommunications refers to the intentional and temporary cessation of providing services by a telecommunications provider.

Name: VTR
Definition: A metric that measures the relationship between the value generated and the time invested in Inbound interaction talk time. Excludes coded time for breaks, statutory holidays, vacation and other activity codes.

Name: W-AGF
Definition: Wireline Access Gateway Function refers to a component in telecommunications systems that performs the task of connecting the customer's premises to the service provider's network. It serves as an interface between the customer's wireline network and the service provider's equipment, allowing for the transmission of voice, data, and other communication services.

Name: WAF
Definition: Web Application Firewall is a security measure implemented in the field of Telecommunications that is designed to protect web applications from various types of cyber threats, such as unauthorized access, data breaches, and malicious attacks. It acts as a barrier between the web application and the internet, monitoring and filtering incoming and outgoing traffic to identify and block any suspicious or malicious activities.

Name: WAN
Definition: A wide area network is a network that serves users across a broad geographic area. A wide area network may be privately owned or rented, but the term usually connotes the inclusion of public (shared user) networks.

Name: WAP
Definition: Wireless Application Protocol is a communication standard in the field of telecommunications. It is used for transmitting and accessing data over wireless networks, specifically designed for mobile devices.

Name: WB-E-UTRAN
Definition: Wide Band E-UTRAN is a telecommunications term that refers to a high-speed wireless network technology used in LTE (Long-Term Evolution) systems. It enables faster data transmission rates and improved network capacity for mobile communication.

Name: WBS
Definition: Work breakdown structure codes are numbers that can be applied to tasks and edit to match the specific needs of your business unit. Project automatically provides basic outline numbers for each task, but you can apply your own customized outline scheme to the project at any time.

Name: WCC
Definition: Wireless Code of Conduct in the context of Enterprise refers to a set of guidelines and rules that govern the use and behavior related to wireless technologies within an organization. It outlines the proper usage, security protocols, and ethical standards that employees must adhere to when using wireless devices and networks in the workplace.

Name: WCDMA
Definition: Wideband Code Division Multiple Access (WCDMA) is a telecommunications technology that allows multiple users to access a wide frequency range simultaneously. It is a method of digital cellular communication that enables the transmission of voice and data over a broad spectrum, increasing the capacity and efficiency of wireless networks.

Name: WFI
Definition: TELUS Applicatoin name

Name: WFM
Definition: Workforce Management refers to the administration and optimization of an enterprise's workforce in order to effectively meet business objectives and operational needs. It involves activities such as scheduling, forecasting, tracking employee time and attendance, and managing labor costs.

Name: WG
Definition: Working Group refers to a collaborative team or committee with a specific task or objective within the context of a general setting.

Name: WHB
Definition: Marketing campaign.

Name: WHP
Definition: Wireless Home Phone refers to a telecommunications service that allows users to make and receive phone calls using a wireless connection within their home.

Name: WHSA
Definition: Wholesale high-speed access services of large cable carriers that enable independent service providers to offer retail Internet services to their own end-users. Sourced from: CRTC wholesale braodband services page

Name: WHSIA
Definition: Wireless High Speed Internet Access refers to a telecommunications technology that allows users to connect to the internet without the need for physical wired connections. It provides fast and reliable internet connections through wireless signals, enabling users to access online services, browse websites, and transmit data quickly and efficiently.

Name: Wi-Fi
Definition: Wireless Fidelity refers to a standard for wireless communication that allows electronic devices to connect to the internet or exchange data without the need for physical wired connections.

Name: WIIFM
Definition: What's In It For Me refers to the individual's primary concern or focus on the personal advantages, benefits, or value that they can gain from a particular situation or decision. It emphasizes a self-centered perspective that is driven by self-interest.

Name: WiMAX
Definition: Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access (WiMAX) is a telecommunications technology that allows for wireless high-speed internet access over large distances, using microwave frequencies.

Name: WLAN
Definition: Wireless Local Area Network refers to a telecommunications technology that enables wireless communication and networking within a limited geographic area, such as an office building, campus, or home.

Full Name: Wireless Local Area Network Control Plane Protocol
Name: WLCP
Definition: Wireless Local Area Network Control Plane Protocol refers to a communication protocol used in telecommunications specifically for controlling and managing the operations of a wireless local area network (WLAN). It is responsible for establishing and maintaining network connections, managing authentication and security processes, handling quality of service (QoS) requirements, and facilitating the overall control and coordination of the network.

Name: WLN
Definition: Wireline in the context of Enterprise refers to a type of communication technology that involves the physical transmission of signals or data through wired connections.

Name: WLS
Definition: Wireless in the context of Enterprise refers to the technology that enables the transmission of data, voice, or video signals without the need for physical cables or wires. It allows for flexible and mobile connectivity within a business environment, facilitating communication and data transfer between devices.

Name: wNGHP
Definition: Wireless Next Generation Home Phone refers to a fixed wireless access voice service that replaces traditional copper landline connections with wireless cellular technology to provide home phone service.

Name: WOID
Definition: Work Order ID is a unique identifier assigned to a specific task or service request that needs to be completed by field technicians or service personnel. Among others used for PureFiber and Home Solutions customers.

Name: WOLA
Definition: Windowed Overlap-and-Add is a signal processing technique used in telecommunications. It involves dividing a longer signal into smaller segments, applying a window function to each segment, and then overlapping and adding these windowed segments together to reconstruct the original signal.

Name: WOW
Definition: Method for evaluating progress over time.

Name: WRC
Definition: World Radio Conference is a global gathering and forum where key stakeholders in telecommunications come together to discuss and establish international regulations and standards for radio communication.

Name: WS
Definition: Wallet Share refers to how much of a customer's expenses for a category of product or service goes to a particular company/brand

Name: WSER
Definition: Workplace Standards Exception Request refers to a formal process within an enterprise where employees can request an exemption or deviation from established workplace standards or policies. These requests are typically made when an employee believes that adhering to certain standards would impede their ability to effectively perform their job responsibilities. The purpose of the request is to seek authorization to deviate from the standard guidelines in order to accommodate specific circumstances or individual needs.

Name: WSG
Definition: Wallet Share Growth is a marketing metric used to calculate the percentage of a customer's spending for a type of product or service that goes to a particular company/brand. A company may use many different strategies and techniques to grow Wallet Share

Name: XG-PON
Definition: Passive Optical Netwrok with (asymmetrical) bandwidth of 10G for downstream and 2.5G for upstream.

Full Name: X Gigabit Symmetrical Passive Optical Network
Name: XGS-PON
Definition: Passive optical network with symmetrical bandwidth of 10G for downstream and 10G for upstream.

Name: XML
Definition: A standard for interchanging meta data.

Name: YE
Definition: Year End in the context of General refers to the end of a calendar year or fiscal year, typically on December 31st. It is a significant date for businesses and organizations as it marks the conclusion of a financial period.

Full Name: Zero touch network and Service Management
Name: ZSM
Definition: Zero touch network and Service Management refers to the automated management and configuration of telecommunications networks and services without any human intervention.
